# 1B.10 Research Note: Biden’s 2024 existential-risk posture

**Bottom line:** **Probably safer than inherited overall, but not by a wide margin.**  
The 2024 record shows substantial institutional build-out around nuclear, cyber, AI, and chem-bio risk, plus repeated de-escalation in major crises. The main offset is that Biden also accepted some controlled military escalation in Ukraine. My comparative judgment is therefore an **inference** from 2024 institutional and crisis-management evidence, not a directly measured before/after score.

## Accepted claims

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Biden-Harris Administration Announces First-Ever Consortium Dedicated to AI Safety](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/02/biden-harris-administration-announces-first-ever-consortium-dedicated-ai) | NIST | 2024-02-08 | https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/02/biden-harris-administration-announces-first-ever-consortium-dedicated-ai | The administration created the U.S. AI Safety Institute Consortium with 200+ stakeholders and tied it to red-teaming, capability evaluations, risk management, and watermarking. This is clear evidence of safer AI governance than a laissez-faire baseline. | `1B.10`, also `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| [U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo Releases Strategic Vision on AI Safety, Announces Plan for Global Cooperation Among AI Safety Institutes](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/us-secretary-commerce-gina-raimondo-releases-strategic-vision-ai-safety) | NIST | 2024-05-21 | https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/us-secretary-commerce-gina-raimondo-releases-strategic-vision-ai-safety | NIST’s AI Safety Institute was launched at Biden’s direction to advance the science of AI safety through scientific cooperation and testing/validation. This strengthens the country’s catastrophic-risk posture in a domain that did not have this institutional scaffolding at the start of the term. | `1B.10`, also `1B.9`, `1B.7` |
| [NIST Launches ARIA, a New Program to Advance Sociotechnical Testing and Evaluation for AI](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/nist-launches-aria-new-program-advance-sociotechnical-testing-and) | NIST | 2024-05-28 | https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/nist-launches-aria-new-program-advance-sociotechnical-testing-and | ARIA was launched to improve testing, evaluation, validation, and verification of AI systems in realistic settings. That is precautionary institutional capacity for a major emerging-risk domain. | `1B.10`, also `1B.9` |

That is direct precaution in one of the clearest catastrophic-risk domains. | `1B.10`, also `1B.9` |

That modestly strengthens the safer-posture case. | `1B.10`, also `1B.9` |

## Counterevidence

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Biden quietly shipped long-range ATACMS to Ukraine](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/the-us-quietly-shipped-longrange-atacms-missiles-to-ukraine-3394976) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-24 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/the-us-quietly-shipped-longrange-atacms-missiles-to-ukraine-3394976 | Secret transfer of long-range missiles increased Ukraine’s strike reach and made the conflict more escalatory. This weakens a pure “safer” reading, though it is still a conventional-war decision rather than a direct existential-risk-policy failure. | `1B.10`, also `1B.8`, `1B.5` |

This is the clearest 2024 “more dangerous” signal I found, but it is still tied to a defensive war. | `1B.10`, also `1B.8`, `1B.5` |

## Synthesis

The best 2024 evidence points to a **net safer existential-risk posture** by the end of Biden’s term than at the start, mainly because the administration built or strengthened:
- AI safety institutions,
- chem-bio AI oversight,
- cyber foresight and hardening,
- nuclear verification and nonproliferation support,
- and formal nuclear command/consultation mechanisms.

The strongest offset is Ukraine policy:
- Biden accepted some controlled escalation and secrecy around long-range weapons.
- That makes the overall judgment less than clean, but it does not outweigh the broader institutional risk-reduction record.

## Search gap

I did **not** find strong 2024 Biden-specific evidence on:
- domestic biological-risk policy beyond chem-bio AI oversight,
- direct AI frontier-model regulation outside safety institutes and NIST guidance,
- or a single comprehensive cross-domain existential-risk strategy.

So the overall call is **inferential**: safer in the aggregate, with real escalation tradeoffs and incomplete coverage outside nuclear/AI/cyber.
